title: Walking to work: The role of walkability around the workplace in a Dutch adult commuting population.
authors: Osmënaj T, Lam TM, Wagtendonk AJ, den Braver NR.
tables: Study population exclusion steps, based on chosen criteria.
Baseline characteristics for participants of OVIN 2017 in total and across quintiles of workplace walkability, presented in n (%) or mean ± SD or median [IQR].

Logistic regression for the associations between (1) quintiles of workplace walkability index at 150m buffer size or (2) continuous workplace walkability (per 10-point increment) and odds of walking for commute. The odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals are presented. N = 6769.

Logistic regression for the association between continuous workplace walkability index at 150m buffer size (per 10-point increment) and odds of walking for commute, stratified by residential urbanization degrees (highly urban, urban, rural). The odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals are presented. N = 6769.

Logistic regression for the association between combined walkability index (residential/workplace) at 150m buffer size and odds of walking for commute. The odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals are presented. N = 6769.
